title: Booking service and strategies
idea: The core design is one BookingService that runs the hold and confirm flows, and talks to seat locks, pricing and payment only through interfaces.

analogy.text: A box office clerk. The clerk follows the same steps every time, but asks the seating desk, the price board and the card machine.
analogy.breaks: Swapping a Java strategy needs no retraining; clerks do.

points: BookingService is a facade: callers see `hold` and `confirm`, nothing else.
`SeatLockProvider` hides where locks live: memory now, PostgreSQL later.
`PricingStrategy` is the strategy pattern: new pricing rules are new classes.
`PaymentGateway` and `Clock` are injected, so tests control money and time.

steps.caption: U-7 asks to hold seats A2 and P1 for show SH-1.
BookingService creates hold id `H-1` and asks for the locks.
The lock provider locks both seats or neither. Both are free.
The service stamps an expiry from the injected `Clock` and returns the hold.
U-9 asks for A1 and A2. A2 is taken, so nothing is locked.
Later U-7 confirms `H-1`. The pricing strategy prices each seat.
The gateway charges the total. Success creates a CONFIRMED Booking.
The Booking returns to the caller. The service never knew how prices were set.

code.title: Service and interfaces
code.caption: The core flow. Every collaborator is an interface passed into the constructor. Booking is trimmed to a record here; page 4 adds the PENDING step and the transition rules.

walk.text: A fixed `Clock` makes the hold expiry the same on every run.
Wire the service with one implementation of each interface.
U-7 holds A2 and P1; U-9 then asks for A1 and A2 and gets neither.
Three interfaces: seat locks, pricing, payment. Each is a swap point.
Locks are all or nothing: check every seat first, then claim them all.
`hold` asks for locks, then records a SeatHold expiring ten minutes later.
`confirm` rejects a missing or expired hold, prices seats, charges, and returns the Booking. Payment failures come later.

code.title: A new strategy
code.caption: A matinee discount added as a new class that wraps any strategy (the decorator pattern). No old class is edited.

walk.text: Wrap the standard pricing with a 20 percent matinee discount.
Price seat A1 for a morning show and an evening show.
The decorator holds the inner strategy and its own percentage.
Before 13:00 it discounts with integer math. A real theatre uses its own time zone.

pitfalls: Do not put `if (matinee)` branches inside BookingService; add a strategy class instead.
Never call `Instant.now()` inside the service; inject a `Clock` so tests are repeatable.
Lock all seats or none; a partial lock leaves orphan seats nobody can buy.

quiz.q: What does MatineePricing print for the morning show?
quiz.why: The show starts at 10:00 UTC, before 13:00. The decorator takes 80 percent of 25000 with long math: 20000.

takeaway: One facade service, with every changing rule behind an injected interface.
